WITH extracted_digits AS (
    SELECT 
        ticker,
        fiscal_year,
        CAST(digit AS INT64) as leading_digit
    FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`stg_sec_filings`,
    -- The core mathematical extraction engine: Grabs the leading digit of ANY number mentioned in the 10-K
    UNNEST(REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(filing_text, r'\b([1-9])\d*')) AS digit
),

digit_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        ticker,
        fiscal_year,
        leading_digit,
        COUNT(*) as digit_freq
    FROM extracted_digits
    WHERE leading_digit > 0 AND leading_digit < 10
    GROUP BY ticker, fiscal_year, leading_digit
),

total_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        ticker,
        fiscal_year,
        SUM(digit_freq) as total_digits
    FROM digit_counts
    GROUP BY ticker, fiscal_year
),

benfords_distribution AS (
    SELECT
        d.ticker,
        d.fiscal_year,
        d.leading_digit,
        d.digit_freq,
        t.total_digits,
        -- Calculate actual frequency % vs expected mathematical curve
        SAFE_DIVIDE(d.digit_freq, t.total_digits) AS actual_distribution,
        LOG10(1 + 1/CAST(d.leading_digit AS FLOAT64)) AS expected_distribution
    FROM digit_counts d
    JOIN total_counts t ON d.ticker = t.ticker AND d.fiscal_year = t.fiscal_year
)

SELECT
    ticker,
    fiscal_year,
    -- A higher sum means the actual numbers deviate further from Benford's biological logarithmic curve (Huge Fraud Risk!)
    SUM(ABS(actual_distribution - expected_distribution)) as benfords_deviation
FROM benfords_distribution
WHERE total_digits > 100 -- Ensure statistical significance of the sample size
GROUP BY ticker, fiscal_year

-- models/marts/fct_narrative_drift.sql

WITH staged_data AS (
    SELECT * FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`stg_sec_filings`
),

drift_calculation AS (
    SELECT
        ticker,
        fiscal_year,
        sentiment_score,
        similarity_index,
        -- Get the similarity from the PREVIOUS year for the same ticker
        LAG(similarity_index) OVER (PARTITION BY ticker ORDER BY fiscal_year) AS prev_year_similarity,
        -- Calculate the "Drift" (Change in narrative)
        similarity_index - LAG(similarity_index) OVER (PARTITION BY ticker ORDER BY fiscal_year) AS similarity_drift
    FROM staged_data
)

SELECT
    *,
    -- Forensic Flag: High similarity but high drift in sentiment is a red flag
    CASE 
        WHEN ABS(similarity_drift) > 0.15 THEN 'HIGH DRIFT'
        WHEN similarity_index > 0.95 THEN 'BOILERPLATE RISK'
        ELSE 'STABLE'
    END AS audit_status
FROM drift_calculation

WITH forensic_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        ticker, 
        fiscal_year,
        sentiment_score,
        -- Note: Ensure subjectivity_score exists in your stg_sec_filings or add it there
        COALESCE(sentiment_score, 0) as sentiment, 
        similarity_index,
        
        -- Calculate a weighted risk score (0 to 100)
        -- High risk = Low Sentiment + High Similarity
        ROUND(
            ((1 - sentiment_score) * 50) + 
            (similarity_index * 50), 2
        ) as risk_score
    FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`stg_sec_filings` -- This creates the link to your Silver layer
)

SELECT 
    *,
    CASE 
        WHEN risk_score > 75 THEN '🔴 CRITICAL: Potential Disclosure Masking'
        WHEN risk_score > 55 THEN '🟡 WARNING: Defensive Reporting'
        ELSE '🟢 LOW: Standard Disclosure' 
    END as audit_priority
FROM forensic_metrics
ORDER BY risk_score DESC

SELECT 
    ticker, 
    COUNT(fiscal_year) as consecutive_boilerplate_years,
    ROUND(AVG(similarity_index), 4) as avg_similarity
FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`fct_narrative_drift`
WHERE similarity_index > 0.95
GROUP BY ticker
HAVING COUNT(fiscal_year) > 3
ORDER BY consecutive_boilerplate_years DESC

WITH engine_a_text AS (
    SELECT * FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`stg_sec_filings`
),

engine_b_financials AS (
    SELECT * FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`stg_financials`
),

benfords_law AS (
    SELECT * FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`fct_benfords_law`
),

text_calculations AS (
    SELECT 
        a.ticker,
        a.fiscal_year,
        a.sentiment_score,
        a.similarity_index,
        -- 1. Disclosure Density (Word count vs Sentiment)
        SAFE_DIVIDE(ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(a.filing_text, ' ')), ABS(a.sentiment_score)) AS density_index,
        
        -- 2. Sentiment Volatility (Looking at standard deviation for the ticker over a trailing 3-year window)
        COALESCE(STDDEV_SAMP(a.sentiment_score) OVER (
            PARTITION BY a.ticker 
            ORDER BY a.fiscal_year 
            ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ), 0.0) AS sentiment_volatility,
        
        -- 3. Narrative Drift (YoY Similarity Change)
        COALESCE(a.similarity_index - LAG(a.similarity_index) OVER (
            PARTITION BY a.ticker ORDER BY a.fiscal_year
        ), 0.0) AS similarity_drift,

        -- Standard word count to maintain compatibility with the Streamlit narrative drift visualization
        ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(a.filing_text, ' ')) AS word_count

    FROM engine_a_text a
)

SELECT 
    t.*,
    COALESCE(b.benfords_deviation, 0.0) AS benfords_deviation,
    COALESCE(f.short_ratio, 0.0) AS short_ratio,
    COALESCE(f.debt_to_equity, 0.0) AS debt_to_equity,
    COALESCE(f.return_on_equity, 0.0) AS return_on_equity,
    COALESCE(f.operating_margin, 0.0) AS operating_margin,
    COALESCE(f.held_institutions, 0.0) AS held_institutions,
    COALESCE(f.insider_ownership, 0.0) AS insider_ownership,
    COALESCE(f.current_ratio, 0.0) AS current_ratio,
    COALESCE(f.quick_ratio, 0.0) AS quick_ratio,
    COALESCE(f.revenue_growth, 0.0) AS revenue_growth,
    COALESCE(f.earnings_growth, 0.0) AS earnings_growth,
    COALESCE(f.profit_margins, 0.0) AS profit_margins,
    COALESCE(f.free_cashflow, 0.0) AS free_cashflow
FROM text_calculations t
-- Join the Benfords Math exactly on same year
LEFT JOIN benfords_law b 
    ON t.ticker = b.ticker AND t.fiscal_year = b.fiscal_year
-- Join the point-in-time Market Financials across all years for that ticker
LEFT JOIN engine_b_financials f 
    ON t.ticker = f.ticker

-- models/marts/fct_anomaly_detection.sql
WITH metrics AS (
    SELECT * FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`int_forensic_metrics`
),
stats AS (
    -- Calculate Industry Averages for Benchmarking
    SELECT 
        AVG(sentiment_score) OVER() as avg_industry_sentiment,
        STDDEV(sentiment_score) OVER() as stddev_sentiment
    FROM metrics
)
SELECT 
    m.*,
    -- Z-Score: (Value - Mean) / StdDev
    -- A Z-score > 2 or < -2 is a statistical anomaly (Red Flag)
    (m.sentiment_score - s.avg_industry_sentiment) / NULLIF(s.stddev_sentiment, 0) as sentiment_z_score
FROM metrics m, stats s

WITH YoY_Sentiment AS (
    SELECT 
        ticker,
        fiscal_year,
        sentiment_score,
        LAG(sentiment_score) OVER (PARTITION BY ticker ORDER BY fiscal_year) as prev_year_sentiment
    FROM `forensic-accounting-bot-491604`.`forensic_data`.`fct_anomaly_detection`
)
SELECT 
    ticker,
    fiscal_year,
    ROUND(sentiment_score, 4) as current_sentiment,
    ROUND(prev_year_sentiment, 4) as prev_year_sentiment,
    ROUND((sentiment_score - prev_year_sentiment), 4) as sentiment_crash
FROM YoY_Sentiment
WHERE prev_year_sentiment > 0 AND sentiment_score < 0 
ORDER BY sentiment_crash ASC
LIMIT 10
